extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, hospital finance officers, Medicare policy stakeholders, and public commenters on CMS rules
extracted.subtask_description: A federal proposed rule describing Medicare Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) and LTCH PPS policies, payment methodologies, quality measure updates, demonstration program requirements, and budget-neutrality methodologies for FY2027; intended to inform providers and solicit public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of substantive measure updates (Clinical Outcomes domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are proposing to adopt substantive measure updates to five condition-specific and procedure-specific mortality measures, in the Clinical Outcome domain, beginning with the July 1, 2028 through June 30, 2030 performance period for the FY 2032 program year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption is contingent on adopting the same refined mortality measures in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program beginning with the FY 2028 payment determination; see section IX.B.2. of the preamble for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to previously adopted Hospital VBP measure sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Summaries of previously adopted measures for the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program are included in prior IPPS/LTCH PPS final rules (e.g., FY 2026 final rule) and summarized in Tables V.J.1 and V.J.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No changes are proposed to the existing measure set for the referenced program years; readers are referred to the cited final rules and tables for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline and performance period schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline and performance periods for the FY 2028 through FY 2032 program years follow the schedule previously finalized in the FY 2017 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables V.J.3 through V.J.7 summarize the previously adopted baseline and performance periods; see FY 2017 final rule (81 FR 56998) for the finalized schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance standards for Clinical Outcomes, Safety, and Efficiency domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously established and newly estimated performance standards exist for measures in the Clinical Outcomes, Safety, and Efficiency and Cost Reduction domains (e.g., MORT-30-AMI, MORT-30-HF, CAUTI, CLABSI, MSPB Hospital).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical Outcomes standards were updated to include COVID-19 patients beginning FY 2027; Safety domain HAI measures will use CY 2022 data to calculate performance standards; MSPB Hospital standards are based on performance period data, so numerical equivalents may not be available at the time of publication. See Table V.J.8 and cited final rules for numeric standards where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCAHPS scoring modification (six unchanged dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring is modified to only score hospitals on the six unchanged Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program dimensions of the HCAHPS Survey until updates to the survey have been publicly reported for one year: 'Communication with Nurses,' 'Communication with Doctors,' 'Communication about Medicines,' 'Discharge Information,' 'Cleanliness and Quietness,' 'Overall Rating.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each of the six dimensions, Achievement Points (0-10) and Improvement Points (0-9) will be calculated; the larger is summed across six dimensions to create pre-normalized HCAHPS Base Score (0-60). Multiply by 8/6 (1.3333333) and round (0.5 and higher up), producing normalized HCAHPS Base Score (0-80). HCAHPS Consistency Points (0-20) calculated same as current method across six dimensions. Final HCAHPS score = Base Score + Consistency Points (range 0-100). Method for calculating performance standards remains unchanged; see Hospital Inpatient Value-Based Purchasing Program final rule (76 FR 26511-26512) for methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of FY 2032 performance standards per codified methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly established performance standards for certain Clinical Outcomes and Efficiency measures for the FY 2032 program year are set out in Table V.J.12 and are based on the methodology codified at 42 CFR 412.160.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance standards for MSPB Hospital are based on performance period data and may not have numeric equivalents at time of proposal; see cited rule text and tables for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: HAC Reduction Program statutory and codified requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The HAC Reduction Program is governed by statutory authority described in earlier IPPS rules and codified at 42 CFR 412.170 through 412.172.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No proposals or updates to the HAC Reduction Program are being made in this proposed rule; references provided for background and for technical specifications maintenance (see FY 2026 final rule citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural Community Hospital (RCH) definition / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A rural community hospital, as defined in section 410A(f)(1), is a hospital that—(1) Is located in a rural area (per section 1886(d)(2)(D)) or treated as rural under section 1886(d)(8)(E); (2) Has fewer than 51 beds (excluding distinct part psychiatric or rehabilitation unit beds) as reported in its most recent cost report; (3) Provides 24-hour emergency care services; and (4) Is not designated or eligible for designation as a CAH under section 1820.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition determines demonstration eligibility and payment methodology applicability for the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory budget neutrality requirement for demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 410A(c)(2) of the MMA requires that aggregate payments made by the Secretary under the demonstration shall not exceed the amount that would have been paid if the demonstration was not implemented (i.e., 'budget neutrality').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically, CMS implemented demonstration budget neutrality either across participants or by offsetting national IPPS rates; the agency interprets statutory language to permit offsetting demonstration costs against national payment rates when appropriate. See historical final rules cited for methods used FY2005–FY2016 and resumed methodology FY2018–FY2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: General budget neutrality methodology components
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget neutrality offsets generally incorporate two components: (1) estimated costs of the demonstration for the upcoming fiscal year (from historical 'as submitted' cost reports for participating hospitals plus updated factors for nationwide trends), and (2) reconciliation amounts representing differences between actual costs (from finalized cost reports) and previously estimated costs, applied to upcoming offsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If actual costs exceed prior estimates, the difference is added to the upcoming estimate; if actual costs are lower, the difference is subtracted. CMS has calculated these differences historically for FYs 2005–2020 and intends to continue the approach for subsequent years when finalized cost reports are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality methodology for CAA, 2021 extension period
rubrics_metrics.description: For the extension period authorized by CAA, 2021, CMS continues the general methodology: estimate upcoming fiscal year demonstration costs based on participating hospitals' historical cost reports and incorporate estimates into budget neutrality offsets to be applied to national IPPS rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to timing and addition of new hospitals, CMS may delay applying offsets (e.g., not proposing an FY 2027 offset in this rule) and instead apply offsets in a later (FY 2028) rule once historical cost reports are available; CMS will also incorporate any statutory changes affecting cost methodology and invites public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital IPPS payment calculation formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic methodology for determining capital prospective payments using the Federal rate is set forth in 42 CFR 412.312 and, for each discharge, the standard Federal rate is adjusted as follows: (Standard Federal Rate) × (DRG Weight) × (Geographic Adjustment Factor (GAF) × (COLA for hospitals located in Alaska and Hawaii) × (1 + Capital DSH Adjustment Factor + Capital IME Adjustment Factor, if applicable)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §412.312(c), hospitals may also receive outlier payments under the capital IPPS for extraordinarily high-cost cases that qualify under established thresholds for each fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception payments under capital IPPS (42 CFR 412.348)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations at 42 CFR 412.348 provide for certain exception payments; regular exception payments in subdivisions (b) through (e) were available only during the 10-year transition period. Special exceptions payments under §412.348(g) ended after FY 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §412.348(f), a hospital may request an additional payment if it incurs unanticipated capital expenditures in excess of $5 million due to extraordinary circumstances beyond the hospital's control. Citations to FY 2005 and FY 2012 final rules provide historical context and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: New hospital definition and capital payment option
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 42 CFR 412.300(b), a 'new hospital' is one that has operated (under previous or current ownership) for less than 2 years; examples of hospitals not considered new are listed in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per §412.304(c)(2), a new hospital is paid 85 percent of its allowable Medicare inpatient hospital capital-related costs through its first 2 years of operation, unless the new hospital elects to receive full prospective payment based on 100 percent of the Federal rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital payments for hospitals located in Puerto Rico (§412.374)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under revised §412.374 (effective for discharges on or after October 1, 2016), capital IPPS payments to hospitals located in Puerto Rico are based on 100 percent of the capital Federal rate, to parallel statutory changes to operating IPPS payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change reflects section 601 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016 (Pub. L. 114-113) which altered the applicable Federal percentage for operating payments to Puerto Rico hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual update to national capital Federal rate (42 CFR 412.308(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed annual update to the national capital Federal rate for FY 2027 is provided in the Addendum to the FY 2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS proposed rule per 42 CFR 412.308(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section III of the Addendum for the proposed update details and calculations; final rate may be revised in the final rule if more current data are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-of-increase update for hospitals excluded from IPPS (target amount methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain hospitals excluded from a prospective payment system (children's hospitals, 11 cancer hospitals, RNHCIs, and hospitals located in certain U.S. territories) are paid on reasonable cost basis subject to a rate-of-increase ceiling; a per discharge target amount is updated annually by a rate-of-increase percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since FY2006 CMS has used the percentage increase in the IPPS operating market basket to update target amounts. For FY2027 CMS estimates the 2023-based IPPS operating market basket increase at 3.2% (per IGI's Q4 2025 forecast) and proposes applying that percentage to update FY2026 target amounts to calculate FY2027 target amounts, subject to use of more recent data for the final rule if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methodology for extended neoplastic disease care hospitals (§412.526)
rubrics_metrics.description: For hospitals classified under section 1886(d)(1)(B)(vi) ('extended neoplastic disease care hospitals'), Medicare allowable net inpatient operating costs are paid on a reasonable cost basis subject to a ceiling determined by multiplying the updated target amount by total Medicare discharges; capital costs paid as described in §412.526(c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cost reporting periods beginning during fiscal years after FY2015, the target amount equals the prior period's target amount updated by the applicable annual rate-of-increase percentage per §413.40(c)(3). For FY2027, CMS proposes using the estimated 3.2% market basket increase to update target amounts, subject to revision with more current data for the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Access Hospital (CAH) certification and payment citations
rubrics_metrics.description: CAH designation is provided under Medicare Rural Hospital Flexibility Programs; CAHs must meet CAH conditions of participation at 42 CFR part 485, subpart F and payments to CAHs are governed by regulations at 42 CFR part 413.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background and program details are provided; specific payment and demonstration-related waivers are discussed in context of demonstration programs (e.g., FCHIP).

rubrics_metrics.name: FCHIP Demonstration eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible entity for the Frontier Community Health Integration Project (FCHIP) Demonstration is a Medicare Rural Hospital Flexibility Program grantee (a CAH) located in a State in which at least 65 percent of the counties in the State have 6 or fewer residents per square mile (per section 123(d)(1)(B) of Pub L. 110-275 as amended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizing statute also required budget neutrality for the demonstration and allowed the Secretary to waive requirements of Titles XVIII and XIX as necessary to carry out the demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCHIP Demonstration budget neutrality and waiver authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 123(g)(1)(B) required the demonstration be budget neutral: aggregate payments made by the Secretary shall not exceed the amount estimated to be paid absent the demonstration. Section 123(i) permits the Secretary to waive Title XVIII/XIX requirements as necessary to implement the demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS used these waivers to allow enhanced payment for telehealth, SNF/NF beds, ambulance services, and home health services in order to increase access without net increase in costs; historical selection and evaluation of participating CAHs is summarized in cited final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention payment and waiver condition (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention payments and payment waiver provisions in the FCHIP Demonstration only apply if the CAH is a participant in the associated intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each CAH may participate in more than one intervention; participation choices affect which waivers and alternative payment methods apply for that CAH during the demonstration extension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telehealth intervention payment methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS waives section 1834(m)(2)(B) of the Act (the originating site facility fee) and modifies the facility fee payment to make reasonable cost-based reimbursement to the participating CAH when it serves as the originating site for a telehealth service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reimburses the participating CAH serving as the originating site at 101 percent of its reasonable costs for overhead, salaries and fringe benefits associated with telehealth services at the participating CAH. This waiver and reimbursement rate apply only to CAHs participating in the telehealth intervention.
